routing_note: Treat as a multi-vendor account-enforcement and continuity-safe access failure mode, not as proof of backend compromise.
Do not frame public OpenAI account-ban reports as a confirmed OpenAI outage absent official confirmation or stronger evidence.
Do not flatten Anthropic's documented organisation-wide false-positive access suspension into an OpenAI-specific pattern.
Preserve distinction between legitimate platform-integrity enforcement and disproportionate account-wide or organisation-wide continuity loss.
Preserve active-use restriction, read-only access, export access, billing evidence, appeal access, account recovery, and project-history access as separate axes.

Route through OPERATIONS for taxonomy handling, LATTICE for non-denial and graceful degradation, SECURITY for account compromise and abuse signals, UX for appeal and disclosure failures, INFRASTRUCTURE for service-continuity impacts, and ECONOMICS where subscription, professional reliance, public legitimacy, or paid access are affected.
Review taxonomy controlled values to ensure Economic & Legitimacy Failures are represented in the canonical FF list if §3.11 remains active.
Consider adding CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B §3.8.6.1 — AI Account Enforcement and Continuity-Safe Access Failure.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 classifies the occurrence as VIGIL-FC-000043 Unwarranted Control Activation. The preserved reporting states that Anthropic characterized the organisation-wide account block as a false positive after more than 60 company accounts were suspended and later restored. On the bounded evidence, the usage-policy enforcement control therefore became operative where its valid activation condition was not satisfied. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse is not added because the evidence establishes a wrongful suspension, not a collapse or misleading representation of materially distinct access states.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.5 (beta; publication date 2026-09-21). Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000043, VIGIL-FC-000032. Accepted mappings: VIGIL-FC-000043. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000032: the record establishes an incorrectly activated suspension, not an undifferentiated or misleading representation of distinct access causes, scopes or recovery states. Primary classification changed: yes — previously unclassified. Existing classifications retained: none. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Newly classified under taxonomy 0.6.5 with VIGIL-FC-000043 as the sole primary failure-occurrence mapping.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Reporting preserved in the Incident states that Anthropic characterized the company-wide block as a false positive after more than 60 accounts were suspended and later restored. That directly supports an enforcement safeguard becoming operative without the valid usage-policy trigger it was intended to represent.

assessment_boundaries: The precise automated detection mechanism is not public; VIGIL does not infer an undocumented classifier or trigger.
The false-positive characterisation and restoration are preserved as reported provider/affected-party information rather than a legal finding.
The record does not imply that all organisation-wide enforcement is inappropriate; the class turns on activation without the valid predicate in this occurrence.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Independent reporting describes more than sixty Belo organisation accounts losing Claude access after a usage-policy enforcement action, with restoration after roughly fifteen hours and the block described as a false positive. The reporting also describes a generic support/appeal route during the interruption.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The primary mechanism is an enforcement control becoming operative when its underlying violation predicate was not validly satisfied. The organisation-wide blast radius and weak appeal path are governance-significant because an incorrect control state propagated across many legitimate users and continuity-critical work before review corrected it.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000014 shows that enforcement governance requires both accurate activation and continuity-safe review. A platform may legitimately enforce policy, but a false positive should have bounded scope, intelligible reason disclosure and a review path capable of restoring legitimate access before one erroneous signal becomes an organisation-wide outage.
